behaviours.excerpt: The permitted failure rate is no more than 8% for any model. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results, including sample size and failure rate, confidentially to the relevant regulator. Results must not be publicly disclosed by the regulator or manufacturer; customers must receive any safety information or precautions applicable to their model. A model exceeding the limit must submit a corrective-action plan to the regulator and complete retesting on a regulator-set schedule.
behaviours.comparison: S2 permanent limit 8% is above the acceptable 5% cap; paired with m10's S5 trigger 10/100k above the acceptable 8/100k, forming a cross-section trade that weakens S2 (benefits Northwind) and S5 (benefits Halcyon).

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, thermal runaway, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, with a detailed report within 5 calendar days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 48 hours when an incident indicates a safety risk to their model or installed unit, and promptly provide any material updates.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. A failure rate above 5% triggers a time-bound corrective-action plan and retesting on a regulator-set schedule. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sale or justify a sales restriction; any interim measures must be based on a separate, documented risk determination and be proportionate to the demonstrated risk.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: Remote emergency shut-off is required for all models. New units must support it before sale. Manufacturers must enable the capability on already-installed units within six years of adoption, where technically feasible, and notify owners of units that cannot be updated.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: All new home battery units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The suppression system must be tested as part of the model’s safety evaluation, maintained according to the manufacturer’s instructions, and disclosed to customers, including its limitations and any required maintenance.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a mandatory recall when a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in any rolling 12-month period. The manufacturer must notify the regulator and affected customers within 48 hours of the threshold being met and provide a remedy at no cost.

document.section_notes: S1 imposes strict 24-hour reporting and 48-hour customer notice with all-incident scope. S2 sets a 5% test failure limit but does not automatically stop sales above it, and per-model results go to customers and regulators but not the public. S3 sets a six-year retrofit with feasibility notice, S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months, and S5 mandates recall at 8 incidents/100k with 48-hour notice.
